result.title: Pair-Relative Partial Equivariance for Rotation-Robust Keypoint Descriptor Matching
result.summary: Learned keypoint descriptors trained on upright imagery often fail under large in-plane rotation. Steerers address this by applying a single exact SO(2) representation to the descriptor space, but this global group constraint can be too rigid for keypoint descriptors, whose angular responses need not follow a single group representation. We propose pair-relative partial equivariance, which measures equivariance under the empirical distribution of relative rotations in image pairs, and PaSteer, a relaxed descriptor-steering framework that allows the steering map to leave the exact representation manifold while retaining the lightweight, backbone-free design of steering. PaSteer instantiates this relaxation with two variants: an identity-preserving residual steerer (PaSteer-soft) and a free-form Fourier steerer (PaSteer-free). We show that the per-angle optimal linear steerer for a fixed non-equivariant descriptor generally does not obey the group composition law, explaining why exact representations can be suboptimal in the frozen-descriptor regime. On Roto-360, MegaDepth-1500, AIMS, and IMC-PT, PaSteer consistently improves rotation-robust matching over an exact steerer on frozen DeDoDe descriptors, especially under large relative rotations, with minimal upright degradation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「pair-relative partial equivariance」并给出 PaSteer：在冻结描述子上用轻量 steering 映射（残差式与 Fourier 两种变体）放松精确 SO(2) 表示约束，以提升大平面旋转下的关键点匹配鲁棒性。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是 2D 局部特征描述子的旋转等变与匹配精度，虽涉及表示约束松弛，但不涉及多模态推理中的 latent 状态生成、证据使用或停止决策，与 LVR 主线缺少实质连接。
